subject: general
question:
Seven students A, B, C, D, E, F, and H give a test. No two students get the same marks. A gets more marks than B. H gets more marks than A. Only two students get more marks than C. D gets more marks than C and B but D doesn't get the highest marks.

If B did not get the lowest marks, then which of the following sequences of their marks is possible?

options.text: H > D > C > E > A > B > F
F > D > C > E > H > B > A
E > C > D > H > A > B > F
H > D > C > B > E > F > A

solution:
Given: Seven students A, B, C, D, E, F, and H give a test.

No two students get the same marks.

1) A gets more marks than B. H gets more marks than A.

H > A > B

2) Only two students get more marks than C

__ > __> C > __ > __ > __ > __

3) D gets more marks than C and B but D doesn't get the highest marks

__ > D > C > __ > __ > __ > __

Given that, If B did not get the lowest marks

Now, After combining statements 1 and 3, we get;

Case 1: __ > D > C > H > A > B > __

Case 2: H > D > C > __ > A > B __ 

Now, checking the options

Option 1: H > D > C > E > A > B > F → **True **(It follows the case 2)

Option 2: F > D > C > E > H > **B > A** → False (It contradicts statement (1) as A > B)

Option 3: E > **C > D** > H > A > B > F → False (It contradicts statement (3) as D > C)

Option 4: H > D > C > **B > E > F > A** → False (It contradicts statement (1) as A > B)

So, Only **H > D > C > E > A > B > F** satisfies the all statements.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option (1)".
